### Factual Comparison of All-NBA Selections

Based on the verified records and evidence:

* **All-NBA First Team:**
  * **LeBron James:** 13 selections (2005–06, 2007–08, 2008–09, 2009–10, 2010–11, 2011–12, 2012–13, 2013–14, 2014–15, 2015–16, 2016–17, 2017–18, 2019–20) [lebron_accolades_160], [T2]
  * **Michael Jordan:** 10 selections (1986–87, 1987–88, 1988–89, 1989–90, 1990–91, 1991–92, 1992–93, 1995–96, 1996–97, 1997–98) [jordan_accolades_160], [T1]

* **All-NBA Second Team:**
  * **LeBron James:** 4 selections (2004–05, 2006–07, 2020–21, 2024–25) [lebron_accolades_240], [T2]
  * **Michael Jordan:** 1 selection (1984–85) [jordan_accolades_160], [jordan_accolades_240], [T1]

* **All-NBA Third Team:**
  * **LeBron James:** 4 selections (2018–19, 2021–22, 2022–23, 2023–24) [lebron_accolades_240], [T2]
  * **Michael Jordan:** 0 selections [T1]

* **Total All-NBA Selections:**
  * **LeBron James:** 21 total selections [T2]
  * **Michael Jordan:** 11 total selections [T1]

---

### Tradeoffs and Analysis

* **Longevity and Sustained All-NBA Status:** LeBron James holds a substantial advantage in total honors (21 to 11) and leads across all three tiers [T1], [T2]. This reflects his sustained elite performance spanning more than two decades, remaining an All-NBA caliber player well into the latter stages of his career [lebron_accolades_240].
* **Peak Concentration:** Michael Jordan's All-NBA profile is concentrated almost entirely at the top tier. Of his 11 career selections, 10 were First Team nods, reflecting a high conversion rate during his active, uninterrupted prime seasons [jordan_accolades_160], [T1].

---

### Subjective GOAT Debate Context

How these statistics are weighed depends on personal criteria rather than objective facts:
* Advocates for **LeBron James** often argue that leading in First Team selections (13 to 10) and total selections (21 to 11) demonstrates unmatched career durability, consistency, and multi-era dominance [T1], [T2].
* Advocates for **Michael Jordan** often place greater emphasis on peak concentration, noting that during his prime Chicago Bulls run, Jordan virtually never fell below First Team honors [jordan_accolades_160], and they argue that accumulating lower-tier selections (Second and Third Teams) late in a career should carry less weight in determining the greatest player of all time.
